summary:
I could not refute any of the record's runtime claims. Every load-bearing number I re-measured matches: HF API sizes, config.json, KV arithmetic, the per-block expert split from a GGUF header range-read, the vLLM registry and the llama.cpp b12407 source.

**vLLM: confirmed it does not fit.** The smallest checkpoint is FP8 at 30.89 GiB, against a 14.65 GiB budget, and Xing is not in the v0.33.0 registry.

**llama.cpp: the recommended setup looks feasible.** Image server-cuda-b12407 with bartowski Q4_K_M (18.68 GiB), --n-cpu-moe 18 and 128k q8_0 K cache:
- GPU weights: 18.676 - 0.465 (token_embd stays on host) - 0.90 (MTP block, not loaded) - 6.63 (experts of blocks 0..17 in RAM) = 10.68 GiB.
- KV: 576 x 34/32 x 40 = 24,480 B/token, so 2.99 GiB at 128k.
- Total about 14.7 GiB, or about 15.0 GiB once the f16 copy of K/V that the flash-attention kernel makes is added (my estimate, below).

**Corrections:**
1. Follow-up PRs #31683 and #31927 are already inside b12407 (247 and 181 commits behind it), not only in b12418.
2. q8_0 K with flash attention at head size 576 is supported in the b12407 source, but it does not use the fast vector kernel. It goes to the MMA kernel, which converts K/V to f16 in temporary memory. My estimate is about 0.3 GiB extra at 128k, which leaves about 0.6 GiB of headroom on 15.92 GiB. Fallback: --n-cpu-moe 20 (9.94 GiB on GPU, about 14.2 GiB total) or 64k context.
3. The speed estimate leaves out MLA cache reads: every decoded token reads the whole cache, 1.49 GiB at 64k and 2.99 GiB at 128k. The 128k bound drops from about 110 to about 80 tok/s, and real decode will be lower as the context fills.
4. The official GGUFs were uploaded before the merge, but their headers already use the mainline layout, so they probably load.

**Tool calling is still the weak point (contested).** The template's call format matches a pattern llama.cpp's generic auto-parser already handles for GLM and Spark2.5, but nobody has tested it with Xing. HF discussion #15 reports that write and edit calls fail on vLLM, and the original poster says they still fail with 65k max_tokens.

**Verdict: usable only after a smoke test.** Run an OpenCode tool-call test, including a multi-argument write, before ranking the model.

verdicts.claim: Checkpoint sizes: BF16 58.14 GiB, FP8 30.89 GiB, W8A8 32.74 GiB; official GGUF iq2_M-slim 10.99, iq3_xxs 13.03, iq3_m 14.39, iq4_xs 17.02, iq4_nl 17.88, IQ4_NL 18.72, q5_0 19.01, q6_k 25.03, q8_0 31.82 GiB; bartowski Q4_K_M 18.68, IQ3_XXS 13.44, IQ2_M 11.67; mradermacher i1-Q4_K_M 17.65, i1-IQ4_XS 15.64, i1-Q3_K_M 13.99. Safetensors param count 31,215,031,088.
verdicts.correction: source-backed (HF API blob sizes summed). bartowski repo createdAt 2026-11-06, README says built with b12174. Also confirmed via https://huggingface.co/api/models/bartowski/XingChen-AGI_Xing4.0-29B-A4B-GGUF?blobs=true and the FP8/w8a8/mradermacher API endpoints.

verdicts.claim: Architecture per config.json: 40 layers, first 2 dense (9216), MoE 1024 x 64 routed + 1 shared, top-4, MLA q_lora 768, kv_lora 512, rope 64, nope 128, v 128, hc_mult 4, 20 Sinkhorn iters, 1 MTP layer, max_position_embeddings 262144 (YaRN 64 x 4096), vocab 131072, untied.
verdicts.correction: direct-statement (raw config.json read). The GGUF header matches: block_count 41 (40 + nextn), head_count_kv 1, key_length 576, value_length 512, context_length 262144, hyper_connection.count 4.

verdicts.claim: KV arithmetic: MLA (512+64) x 40 layers = 46,080 B/token BF16/f16, 23,040 FP8 (vLLM), 24,480 B/token q8_0 in llama.cpp; 64k q8_0 = 1.49 GiB, 128k = 2.99 GiB; f16 64k 2.81 GiB.
verdicts.correction: source-backed: 576 x 2 x 40 = 46,080; 576/32 x 34 x 40 = 24,480; 131072 x 24,480 = 2.99 GiB. xing4-0.cpp calls build_attn(inp_attn_k, ...): K-only cache. The KV cache covers the 40 trunk layers (n_layer), and the MTP layer adds one more only with --mtp.

verdicts.claim: vLLM: does not fit on 16 GB; Xing4_0ForCausalLM not in the v0.33.0 registry (only TeleChat/TeleChat2/TeleChat3); support only through out-of-tree xing4-vllm-plugin pinned to commit 2e09247; mHC requires bfloat16.
verdicts.correction: source-backed: registry grep shows only TeleChat2ForCausalLM, TeleChat3ForCausalLM and TeleChatForCausalLM. Plugin README (gh api repos/XingChen-AGI/xing4-vllm-plugin/readme) names commit 2e09247c2d7b and says mHC (hc_mult > 1) requires bfloat16. Budget 14.65 - 30.89 - 1.2 = -17.44 GiB. CPU offload is not a path (KB: #66264).

verdicts.claim: llama.cpp b12407 supports xing4_0 (src/llama-arch.cpp line 93), PR #31589 merged 2026-11-05T16:47:27Z as 45b6604, b12407 is 251 commits ahead; follow-ups #31683 and #31927 landed by b12418; MTP tensors skipped unless --mtp.
verdicts.correction: Minor: #31683 (merged 2026-11-05, 6023692b1) and #31927 (merged 2026-11-09, a8fad21e9) are both already in b12407 (gh compare: 247 and 181 commits ahead, 0 behind), not only in b12418. --mtp exists at common/arg.cpp:3086 at b12407, and xing4-0.cpp:91-92 sets TENSOR_SKIP on MTP tensors when load_mtp is false.

verdicts.claim: Q4_K_M offload plan: 17.31 GiB would be on GPU; --n-cpu-moe 18 puts 6.63 GiB of experts in RAM and leaves 10.68 GiB on GPU; with 128k q8_0 KV (2.99) and about 1 GiB compute, about 14.7 GiB VRAM; --n-cpu-moe 14 gives 12.16 GiB GPU / 5.16 GiB RAM.
verdicts.correction: source-backed: parsed from a 12 MB header range-read. Total 18.676 GiB, token_embd Q8_0 0.465, MTP block 0.90, trunk experts 15.03 GiB. Experts per block: 0.482 (blocks 2-3), 0.453 (4-9), 0.369 (10-38), 0.644 (39). Blocks 0..17 = 6.63 GiB, 0..13 = 5.16 GiB, 0..19 = 7.37 GiB. The 14.7 GiB total leaves out the f16 temporary copy of K/V the MMA flash-attention kernel makes (about 0.15 + 0.13 GiB at 128k), so the real figure is about 15.0 of 15.92 GiB. Tight but probably fits. Safer: --n-cpu-moe 20 (9.94 GiB on GPU, about 14.2 GiB total, 7.84 GiB host RAM).

verdicts.claim: q8_0 K cache with flash attention for MLA head 576 on sm_120 is unverified.
verdicts.correction: Narrowed by source reading. Q8_0 is in ggml_cuda_fattn_kv_type_supported, and case 576 accepts V=512 with gqa_opt (gqa ratio 32/1). Because 576 > 256 the vector kernel is never used, so sm_120 gets BEST_FATTN_KERNEL_MMA_F16, which converts the quantized K/V to f16 in temporary memory. It is a supported path, not a failure, but costs extra memory and time (see KB #27623). It is still unmeasured on this machine.

verdicts.claim: Official XingChen GGUF iq2_M-slim works as an all-on-GPU alternative on mainline.
verdicts.correction: The files were uploaded 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-23, before the 11-05 merge. The parsed header still uses the mainline layout and keys: attn_k_b/attn_v_b, hc_attn_*/hc_ffn_*, hyper_connection.*, and the same KV keys as bartowski's file. The vendor README says b12174+ loads them. Likely loads, but not run here. Budget 10.99 - 0.465 - 0.52 MTP = about 10.0 GiB, plus 2.99 + 1 + 0.3 = about 14.3 GiB at 128k.

verdicts.claim: Tool calling in llama.cpp uses the generic auto-parser (TAG_WITH_TAGGED); there is no xing file in common/parsers at b12407; working is inferred and untested.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed that common/parsers at b12407 has no xing file. Xing's format <tool_call>name<param_key>k</param_key><param_value>v</param_value></tool_call> follows the same pattern as formats autoparser.md lists as handled: GLM-4.6/4.7 and Spark2.5 (<tool_call>name<arg_key>...<arg_value>...). That makes it plausible, but still inferred. The template calls _args.items(), so it needs object-form arguments.

verdicts.claim: HF discussion #15: write and edit tool calls fail in agent harnesses on vLLM FP8; a responder attributed it to thinking plus max_tokens truncation inside param_value; the original user says it still fails at 65k output.
verdicts.correction: contested: verified in the discussion API events (2026-10-29 report, xiongji reply the same day, OP reply 2026-11-05 that it still fails with 65536 max output). The thread is still open.

verdicts.claim: Recommended configuration (llama.cpp b12407, bartowski Q4_K_M, --n-cpu-moe 18, -c 131072, -ctk q8_0) serves OpenCode with at least 64k context.
verdicts.correction: Memory: feasible on paper with about 0.6 GiB headroom. Most realistic config: the same command with --n-cpu-moe 20, or -c 65536 if startup reports OOM. Needs the NVIDIA Container Toolkit with CDI first. The 64k+ context target is met. Working tool calls are unproven: auto-parser untested, plus the #15 report. Gate the model on an OpenCode multi-argument write/edit smoke test with thinking both on and off.

verdicts.claim: Speed: Q4_K_M with --n-cpu-moe 18 has a bound of about 110 tok/s (3.0 GB VRAM + 0.45 GB DDR5 per token), expect 40-70 tok/s.
verdicts.correction: inferred. The bound leaves out MLA cache reads, which grow with context: each decoded token reads the whole cache, 1.49 GiB at 64k and 2.99 GiB at 128k. At a full 128k context the bound is (3.0 + 3.2 GB)/896 GB/s = 6.9 ms, plus 5.6 ms from DDR5, about 80 tok/s. Expect throughput to fall as the session context grows. The PR reports H800 tg128 iq4_nl 159 tok/s.

verdicts.claim: Ollama: no library tag; v0.40.16 pins llama.cpp b12177, which is after the merge.
verdicts.correction: LLAMA_CPP_VERSION = b12177, and the merge commit 45b6604 is 21 commits behind b12177. ollama.com/library/xing4 returns 404. Load, tool and think behaviour remain unknown.
